hermetic_exceptions.reason: The affected-set gate is an orchestrator that invokes the owned Buck2 build/test boundary to compute the admission cone; the predicate result is derived from Buck2 reports, not ad-hoc shell policy.
hermetic_exceptions.cutover_note: Replace the subprocess edge with the typed cloud-ci runner/reconciler API when that API owns Buck2 execution; keep the exception visible until then.

hermetic_exceptions.reason: The firewall app uses wall time only to stamp human-reviewed signoff metadata; the gate verdict is computed from the candidate and frozen baseline data, not from the clock.
hermetic_exceptions.cutover_note: Move signoff metadata stamping behind the typed audit packet producer so verifier code stays clock-free; verdict code must remain independent of this exception.

hermetic_exceptions.reason: Freshness is the generated-face regeneration orchestrator: it invokes owned Buck2-built emitters/producers and compares regenerated bytes to the candidate tree. Current shell-outs are transitional and explicitly baselined instead of silently allowed.
hermetic_exceptions.cutover_note: Drive regeneration and SCM facts through the typed Buck2/reconciler API plus scm-facts emitter contract, then delete Command::new from freshness production code.

hermetic_exceptions.reason: Freshness SystemTime::now is restricted to unique temporary file names for scm-facts, volatile facts, masterplan projection, and product graph scratch files; it does not feed the regenerated bytes comparison or pass/fail verdict.
hermetic_exceptions.cutover_note: Replace temp-name wall-clock entropy with the typed scratch allocator when the reconciler API lands; until then, keep every SystemTime::now occurrence in temporary_* helpers only.

hermetic_exceptions.reason: Kernel-purity invokes cargo metadata only after its fixer edits manifests so corrupt rewrites roll back; the blocking gate predicate remains policy/data driven and Buck2-tested.
hermetic_exceptions.cutover_note: Move semantic manifest validation behind the owned workspace-members/manifest parser so the fixer rollback path no longer shells to cargo.

policy_literal_exceptions.reason: The freshness rust-toolchain drift helper names the cloud-kernel nested workspace as a current repo exception while checking workspace toolchain drift; this is current-shape inventory, not readiness semantics.
policy_literal_exceptions.cutover_note: Move nested-workspace skip paths into the freshness policy data when the typed toolchain drift contract is split from the orchestrator.

no_autofix_reason.oya-cloud-ci-affected-set-app: The admission cone is computed from changed targets and Buck2 reports; remediation depends on the source change and cannot be rewritten safely by the gate.
no_autofix_reason.oya-cloud-ci-authz-coverage-app: Unauthenticated control-plane findings require product authorization design changes; the baseline writer is review-gated and not a safe automatic fix.
no_autofix_reason.oya-cloud-ci-automation-ratchet-app: Automation-ratchet findings require choosing the durable automation owner and cannot be mechanically rewritten from observation rows.
no_autofix_reason.oya-cloud-ci-bnf-layer-suffix-app: Crate naming and layer placement are design decisions; an automatic rename would break imports, manifests, and ownership without review.
no_autofix_reason.oya-cloud-ci-cache-wiring-app: Cache topology violations require runner/cache policy decisions, so the gate reports exact wiring gaps instead of mutating CI configuration.
no_autofix_reason.oya-cloud-ci-canonical-json-app: This gate already ships an explicit --fix path; the policy reason remains as documentation for adopters that disable rewriting.
no_autofix_reason.oya-cloud-ci-capability-membership-app: Capability membership gaps require source-of-truth registry ownership decisions, not a blind generated mapping.
no_autofix_reason.oya-cloud-ci-cargo-prefix-app: Prefix violations are migration-sensitive naming decisions; remediation is a reviewed rename or neutral-profile policy change.
no_autofix_reason.oya-cloud-ci-catalog-liveness-app: Catalog liveness findings require either restoring a crate or explicitly marking the catalog row non-live; the gate cannot infer intent.
no_autofix_reason.oya-cloud-ci-cedar-deploy-parity-app: Cedar deployment parity findings require authored policy changes or deployed ConfigMap fixes, both security-sensitive human decisions.
no_autofix_reason.oya-cloud-ci-cross-artifact-agreement-ap: Cross-artifact contradictions must be resolved at the authoritative artifact, never guessed by an automatic rewrite.
no_autofix_reason.oya-cloud-ci-crypto-backend-purity-app: Crypto backend activation changes are security-sensitive dependency choices and cannot be rewritten safely by the gate.
no_autofix_reason.oya-cloud-ci-dependency-automation-app: Dependency automation policy violations require ownership of the dependency update surface, not automatic config synthesis.
no_autofix_reason.oya-cloud-ci-dto-authz-trust-app: Caller-supplied authorization trust findings require server-side PDP integration, not a mechanical baseline expansion.
no_autofix_reason.oya-cloud-ci-embedded-asset-hermeticity-: Embedded asset findings require BUCK src mapping or source layout changes, which are repo-shape decisions.
no_autofix_reason.oya-cloud-ci-enforcement-liveness-app: Enforcement liveness failures require wiring real hook/settings/controller surfaces; the gate cannot safely invent enforcement.
no_autofix_reason.oya-cloud-ci-firewall-app: Firewall ratchet failures require reducing the violating keys or reviewed signoff; automatic mutation would launder debt.
no_autofix_reason.oya-cloud-ci-freshness-app: Freshness failures require regenerating generated faces from authoritative sources or fixing the source drift; automatic mutation is separated into explicit materializer binaries.
no_autofix_reason.oya-cloud-ci-friction-accounting-app: Friction accounting findings require valid ledger semantics and owner routing; the gate cannot invent remediation ownership.
no_autofix_reason.oya-cloud-ci-gate-self-conformance-app: Gate self-conformance findings require changing gate code, Buck2 wiring, workflow registration, or policy exceptions; automatic rewrites would hide the review decision.
no_autofix_reason.oya-cloud-ci-generated-artifact-control-: Generated artifact policy findings require classifying artifact authority and generated-path ownership, not blind path edits.
no_autofix_reason.oya-cloud-ci-hyperscaler-parity-taxonomy: Hyperscaler taxonomy gaps are product-readiness classification decisions and must be resolved in the taxonomy source.
no_autofix_reason.oya-cloud-ci-kernel-purity-app: Kernel-purity ships a fixer for dependency declarations, but topology and semantic validation failures still require reviewed source changes.
no_autofix_reason.oya-cloud-ci-manifest-hygiene-app: Manifest hygiene findings require package metadata and ownership decisions; the gate reports exact missing fields for reviewed repair.
no_autofix_reason.oya-cloud-ci-planned-maturity-app: Planned-maturity findings require authored PRD traceability, rich capability records, or explicit retired-plan provenance/live-ref decisions; the gate must not invent readiness evidence.
no_autofix_reason.oya-cloud-ci-no-graphql-without-adr-app: GraphQL reintroduction requires an explicit reversing ADR or removal; the gate cannot author that decision automatically.

no_autofix_reason.oya-cloud-ci-target-parity-app: Target parity findings require build/test target wiring decisions and cannot be inferred safely from one file.
no_autofix_reason.oya-cloud-ci-tier-dependency-acyclicity-: Tier dependency findings require topology changes across capability boundaries, not automatic rewrites.
no_autofix_reason.oya-cloud-ci-tier-field-coverage-app: Tier field coverage findings require choosing authoritative service tier metadata.
